# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 7 (Bu-Vb Np7)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np7
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 7
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 7. Accepting too many robes
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-np7
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tatuttari-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 7) governs the proper conduct of Buddhist monastics when accepting robe material after their robes have been stolen, lost, or destroyed [Hirakawa 1982; SuttaCentral]. The rule specifies that under such circumstances a monastic may ask for robe-cloth but must show moderation; if multiple robes are offered, he or she may accept no more than two [Hirakawa 1982; SuttaCentral]. If a monk accepts more than the permissible limit, he must forfeit the excess robe-cloth and confess the transgression (*nissaggiya pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. In the Pāli tradition, this disciplinary regulation applies to both monks and nuns, being held in common and omitted as a separate rule within the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga proper [Hirakawa 1982]. Modern English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this rule is shared across virtually all surviving monastic lineages, including the Bhikkhupātimokkha, the Parivāra, and the Vinayas and Prātimokṣa sūtras of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, and Dharmaguptaka traditions, as well as in Gāndhārī fragments and corresponding Bhikkhunī Vinaya codes (such as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga NP 17) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus confirms substantial cross-linguistic alignment with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-4), Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra*, and related commentaries [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects extensive internal Pāli text reuse, particularly with the *Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi* commentary (*Vin04t*) and formulaic phrasing shared across other robe-related Nissaggiya Pācittiya rules (such as NP 6, NP 8, NP 9, and NP 27) [DharmaNexus].
